fig1: Fig. 1. Workflow for evaluating maize phenology models in the German monitoring network. (a) Model performance using all eligible historical training data. (b) Local calibration with historical observations. (c) Transfer among annual-temperature zones and a pooled training control. (d) Weather-product substitution and recalibration. Model training, selection, residual corrections and normalization use pre-2011 data. Paired comparisons share target observations within each experiment; training budgets and cohorts differ among experiments. Local calibration uses five models and one fixed training sample. Annual temperature defines transfer zones; April–September climate determines blend weights.
fig2: Fig. 2. Geographic coverage of maize observations and evaluation cohorts. (a) Distinct observed years during 1981–2025. (b) Quintiles of 1981–2010 mean annual temperature, ordered from coldest to warmest. Panels (a, b) cover 2,232 monitoring sites. (c) Eligibility for local-calibration and weather comparisons among 1,029 held-out sites; categories are mutually exclusive. Markers indicate weather grid-cell centres; blank areas are unsampled. Only centres inside Germany are displayed, while numerical summaries retain the full cohort. Panels share EPSG:3035, extent and one scale bar. Boundaries: Natural Earth 1:50m.
fig3: Fig. 3. Stage-specific prediction errors. (a) MAE. (b) Bias, defined as predicted minus observed date; negative values indicate earlier predictions. Models use all eligible 1981–2010 training observations and valid 2011–2025 test predictions. Colours and values are in days. Physiological maturity corresponds to BBCH 87. Confidence intervals and sample sizes accompany the plotting data.
fig4: Fig. 4. Geographic distribution of prediction errors within Germany. (a, b) T and nonlinear-T MAE at flowering onset (BBCH 61), respectively. (c) MLP-minus-nonlinear-T MAE at flowering onset. (d–f) Corresponding quantities at physiological maturity (BBCH 87). Negative differences favour MLP. Squares show weather grid-cell averages; crosses mark cells with invalid or unresolved predictions, which are excluded from MAE. Models use common 2011–2025 targets and all eligible historical training observations; paired differences use common valid predictions. Colours saturate above 30 d for MAE and beyond ±10 d for differences. Only centres inside Germany are displayed; summaries retain the full cohort. Blank areas are unsampled. Panels share EPSG:3035, extent and one 200-km scale bar. Boundaries: Natural Earth 1:50m.
fig5: Fig. 5. Effects of local calibration. (a) MAE. (b) Bias after 0, 1, 3 or 5 years of local observations. Lines show stage-balanced means and shading shows conditional 95% confidence intervals. Calculations use valid predictions on the 822-site test cohort; paired contrasts use observations valid at both calibration levels. The five models share training sites, local-year budgets and the date-adjustment method.
fig6: Fig. 6. Transfer errors among annual-temperature zones. (a) T. (b) Nonlinear T. (c) Residual RF. (d) Residual MLP. (e) Thermal Transformer. (f) Support blend. Zones 1–5 are quintiles of 1981–2010 mean annual temperature, ordered from coldest to warmest. Cells show excess MAE (d): error after training in the source zone minus error after training in the target zone, using common valid 2011–2025 predictions. Positive values indicate higher error; diagonals are zero. Each fit uses 40 sites and eight historical years per site, with three training samples in each of five spatial folds. Stages receive equal weight; prediction failures are reported separately.
fig7: Fig. 7. Transfer errors at physiological maturity (BBCH 87) within Germany. (a–c) Coldest-zone training for nonlinear T, MLP and the support blend, respectively. (d–f) Warmest-zone training for the same models. Excess MAE (d) subtracts the error after target-zone training on common valid 2011–2025 predictions; positive values indicate higher error. Values average three training samples and monitoring sites within weather grid cells. Each fit uses 40 sites and eight historical years per site. Crosses mark cells with invalid predictions from either model in the contrast; failures receive no numerical error penalty. Colours saturate beyond ±30 d. Only centres inside Germany are displayed; summaries retain the full cohort. Blank areas are unsampled. Panels share EPSG:3035, extent and one scale bar. Boundaries: Natural Earth 1:50m.
fig8: Fig. 8. Prediction performance across climatic distance. (a) Sites with valid nonlinear-T comparisons. (b) MAE. (c) Bias. The horizontal axis is target minus training-median annual temperature; negative values indicate colder targets. Points aggregate fixed distance bins, and shading shows conditional 95% confidence intervals. Counts are not additive because sites can occur in several comparisons. The far-cold bin contains nine sites. The two directions involve different target populations.
fig9: Fig. 9. DWD station and ERA5-Land reanalysis temperatures (0.1° grid). (a) Daily mean temperature, (Tmin + Tmax)/2. (b) Diurnal temperature range, Tmax − Tmin. Colours count distinct grid-cell/calendar-day pairs in 1 °C bins; dashed lines indicate equality. Overlapping weather windows from different sowing dates are counted once. Some grid cells share DWD stations. Both products use qualified 00–24 UTC days; differences also reflect the spatial representation of station and grid temperatures.
fig10: Fig. 10. Effects of weather inputs on prediction errors. (a, b) Changes in MAE and bias after substituting weather without refitting, relative to each model’s original product. (c, d) DWD-minus-ERA5 changes in MAE and bias after product-specific refitting. Points and lines show paired means and conditional 95% confidence intervals on shared valid observations. Positive bias changes indicate later predictions. Training uses 40 sites and four years per site; test observations span 2011–2024. Resampling accounts for shared stations and spatial blocks.
figs1: Fig. S1. Absolute errors in the climatic-transfer experiment. (a) T. (b) Nonlinear T. (c) Residual RF. (d) Residual MLP. (e) Thermal Transformer. (f) Support blend. Zones 1–5 are quintiles of 1981–2010 mean annual temperature, ordered from coldest to warmest. Cells show MAE (d) among valid 2011–2025 predictions, with equal stage weights. Each fit uses 40 sites and eight historical years per site, with three training samples in each of five spatial folds. Prediction failures are reported separately. Fig. 6 shows excess error relative to target-zone training.
